$what-an-entry-is: A licence for ONE test, keyed by its TEST NAME, to fail without failing CI.
$rules: A failure that is NOT on this list fails the gate. That is the whole point of the gate.
The list may only SHRINK. If a listed test PASSES, the gate fails until the entry is deleted — so a fix and its deletion land in the same PR.

Every reason must name a mechanism: what the test binds, spawns, writes, reads, or assumes about the machine or the calendar. The loader REJECTS the words 'flaky', 'intermittent' and 'unstable' — a failure with no named mechanism is indistinguishable from a real regression, which is how a real regression hides.

A test that is genuinely nondeterministic cannot satisfy the shrink-only ratchet, so it may set "nondeterministic": true to opt out of it. That is a bigger licence and costs more: such an entry MUST carry "tracking" (the issue where the defect is being fixed) and "expires" (an ISO date after which the gate fails). A quarantine with no meter is a parking space.

$fields.test: the test name exactly as the runner reports it — this is the key
$fields.file: repo-relative path, for the reader; cross-checked whenever the runner reports file attribution
$fields.reason: the mechanism — at least 40 characters, and not the word 'flaky'
$fields.nondeterministic: optional; true opts the entry out of the shrink-only ratchet
$fields.tracking: required when nondeterministic — the issue tracking the fix
$fields.expires: required when nondeterministic — ISO date after which this entry fails the gate

entries.reason: DETERMINED, and deliberately still listed. Runs only where pwsh is on PATH, which ubuntu-latest has and a typical macOS checkout does not, so it skips locally and runs in CI. `exit 7` is a PowerShell LANGUAGE statement, not a native exit status: inside `& { ... }` it terminates the whole host before the __DFW_END_ sentinel line executes, so stdout is empty. Probed against pwsh 7.4.2 (mcr.microsoft.com/powershell) on 2026-09-23: (a) `try { & { exit 7 } } finally { ... }` DOES run the finally, so the sentinel CAN be made to survive, but $LASTEXITCODE is empty there and execution still stops afterwards; (b) a separate runspace ([powershell]::Create().AddScript('exit 7').Invoke()) survives the host but also yields no exit code, in the runspace or outside it; (c) only a CHILD pwsh (`& pwsh -NoProfile -Command <cmd>`) sets $LASTEXITCODE to 7. So PowerShell exposes the value passed to `exit` to nothing in-session, and the only fix is to run every dispatch in a child process — which ends the long-lived session that is the daemon's entire purpose: cwd, PowerShell variables, functions, aliases and any $env: the command sets would stop persisting across dispatches (env flows parent to child only). Reporting one exit code correctly is not worth losing session state, so the gap stands and the test stays red rather than being weakened to match it. Note the same statement has the same effect in bash — `{ exit 7 ; }` exits that shell too — so this is a limitation of the in-session sentinel protocol, not of wrappers/powershell.cjs specifically; there is simply no bash test asserting it. Issue #95.

$why-the-key-is-the-name: Not file::name, which was the first design. node 22's junit reporter emits no testcase file attribute and node 25's does, so a file-based key resolves differently on a developer's machine and on the runner — the list would appear to shrink locally and silently fail to match in CI. The name is identical on every version. The cost is ambiguity, and it is paid explicitly: the gate FAILS when a listed name matches more than one test in the run.
$environment: This list describes the GATE's environment: ubuntu-latest + node 22, as pinned in .github/workflows/test.yml. Entries can be platform-specific and PASS or SKIP on macOS, so a developer running scripts/ci-unit-gate.cjs locally may see the shrink-only ratchet complain that a listed test 'PASSED this run'. That is expected: the gate is a CI gate, and the ratchet is evaluated against CI. The reverse is the trap — a Linux-only failure is invisible on a macOS checkout — and `docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/src:ro node:22 bash -c 'cp -a /src /repo && cd /repo && rm -rf node_modules && npm ci && node --test <file>'` reproduces the runner's bash 5.2 / readline 8.1 environment locally. That is how the five bracketed-paste entries were reproduced and cleared.
